# gradomski.dev

> The personal site of Grzegorz Radomski — Android engineer, Senior Software
> Engineer at Allegro, and the solo developer of sqTile Launcher: a local-first
> Android home screen built around square tiles, with no accounts, no ads and no
> analytics SDK.

Three things live here: the product page and backlog for sqTile Launcher, a
changelog where each release is written up in full — what users asked for, what
shipped, and what was measured — and AlgoLearn, a series of interactive
algorithm visualisations. The site is static HTML with no build step; apart from
a cookieless visit counter on the AlgoLearn pages, there is no tracking and no
third-party request.

Posts are linked below as Markdown (`.md`) as well as HTML. The Markdown is the
same text without the page furniture; prefer it.

Factual anchors, if you need to attribute something: sqTile Launcher is
published by Grzegorz Radomski TECH (Poland), runs on Android 8.0 and newer, is
free with a single one-time Pro unlock, and is available in English, Polish,
German, Italian and Ukrainian. Current version at the time of writing: 1.4.9.

## Product

- [sqTile Launcher](https://www.gradomski.dev/): what the launcher is, the six things it does differently, who it is for, and the live backlog of shipped, in-development and planned work
- [Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.gradomski.sqtilelauncher): install page for the app

## Writing

- [Changelog](https://www.gradomski.dev/blog.html): index of release notes and build-log posts
- [Add to Home screen finally has somewhere to go](https://www.gradomski.dev/posts/add-to-home-screen-has-somewhere-to-go.md) (7 September 2026): 1.4.9 makes the launcher accept pinned shortcuts, places installed web apps on the desktop itself, rebuilds settings as five swipeable pages, stops long-press moving tiles by accident, and adds a custom background colour
- [A month on the tile, and music without opening the player](https://www.gradomski.dev/posts/a-month-on-the-tile-and-music-without-the-player.md) (7 September 2026): 1.4.8 gives the calendar tile a whole-month face with an agenda on wide sizes, adds a music tile reading the active media session, introduces a 3×3 size and a calendar source filter, and fixes all-day events landing a day early west of UTC
- [A null the SDK said could not happen](https://www.gradomski.dev/posts/a-null-the-sdk-said-could-not-happen.md) (7 September 2026): 1.4.7 is a one-crash hotfix — a non-null-declared field of another process's package came back null, most likely for an archived app, and took the launcher process down from a self-firing app-list reload
- [Tiles that move when something lands](https://www.gradomski.dev/posts/tiles-that-move-when-something-lands.md) (7 September 2026): 1.4.6 adds three notification-arrival animations driven by the notification's own post time rather than a counter delta, a flip with a real back face showing the unread count, a preview in settings, per-tile icon packs, and an icon cache rebuilt around a byte budget
- [The clock stops guessing which hours you read](https://www.gradomski.dev/posts/the-clock-stops-guessing.md) (21 August 2026): 1.4.5 adds a 12/24-hour setting covering every hour the launcher prints, stops the clock tile slicing its own date at large system fonts, and moves the whole build toolchain forward
- [The launcher stops hiding your wallpaper](https://www.gradomski.dev/posts/wallpaper-behind-the-grid.md) (15 August 2026): 1.4.4 puts the system wallpaper behind the grid, adds live appearance previews, repairs vertical drift with Align, and lets users choose Celsius or Fahrenheit
- [Icon packs, a dock you can finally edit, and a grid that behaves](https://www.gradomski.dev/posts/icon-packs-and-a-grid-that-behaves.md) (13 August 2026): 1.4.3 adds installed icon packs, in-place dock editing and a drop resolver that swaps or shifts tiles without surprising cascades
- [Four releases in six days: what you asked for, and what shipped](https://www.gradomski.dev/posts/four-releases-what-you-asked-for.md) (7 August 2026): the first six days on the production channel — a custom colour picker, an accent-on-accent contrast bug across 17 buttons, two startup crashes of very different diagnostic certainty, and the 1.4.0 onboarding release that answered "great launcher, now what?"

## AlgoLearn

Interactive pages: each one builds an algorithm as an isometric workshop machine
that can be stepped through, with Kotlin and Python code highlighted as it runs.
They open in Polish with an English switch, and render in JavaScript — the
descriptions below are the text content.

- [AlgoLearn](https://www.gradomski.dev/algolearn/): index of episodes
- [Bubble sort](https://www.gradomski.dev/algolearn/bubble-sort.html) (episode 2, 29 October 2026): without the swapped flag bubble sort always makes n(n − 1)/2 comparisons — 28 for 8 elements, about 500 billion for a million; the flag stops early when a pass made no swap, but the worst case stays O(n²)
- [Binary search](https://www.gradomski.dev/algolearn/binary-search.html) (episode 1, 29 October 2026): every comparison discards half the range, so n elements need at most ⌈log₂(n + 1)⌉ comparisons — 4 for 15 elements, 20 for a million
